title: New Tattoo Ink Can Vanish and Come Back
summary:
Most tattoos stay the same forever. But engineers at the University of Colorado Boulder are making a new ink that can disappear and then come back.

The ink changes because of light. When ultraviolet, or UV, light hits it, the color fades until you can no longer see it. When normal light hits it later, the color returns. It works a bit like glasses that get darker in the sun.

The ink comes in three colors: yellow, blue and magenta. Each color is made of tiny beads. Inside the beads are special chemicals that react to light.

One of the inventors, scientist Carson Bruns, tested the ink on his own leg over about 12 months. All the colors worked as planned, and the ink kept working for more than two years.

The team hopes doctors might one day use it to make temporary marks on skin. For now, the ink is only for lab use until more safety tests are done.
why_it_matters: It shows how science can make materials that change with light, like glasses that get darker in the sun.
